newsitem.title: USA: Sunbeam facts at a glance.
newsitem.headline: Sunbeam facts at a glance.

text.p: Sunbeam Corp. Tuesday announced a major restructuring that will cut about 6,000 workers, slash product lines and close 39 plants and other facilities. This is what Sunbeam looks like today:
Products: Sunbeam brand blenders, mixers, clocks, timers, warming blankets, bath scales and heating pads; Oster mixers and blenders; Sunbeam barbecues, patio furniture and hair care products.

Earnings: $50.5 million, or 61 cents a share, on sales of about $1.20 billion in 1995, compared with $107 million, or $1.30 a share, on sales of $1.20 billion in 1994. Reported first quarterly loss since going public in the third quarter.

History: Sunbeam is the successor to the consumer products business of Allegheny International Inc. In 1992, an outside investment group bought Sunbeam assets from the bankrupt Allegheny and later that year took the company public.
Corporate turnaround specialist Albert Dunlap, named chairman in July 1996, pledged to overhaul company within a year.
